data.detailed_description:
1982 is a FREE retro inspired blasta-thon that will test your gaming skills to the max.

The game was created using AppGameKit an easy, quick and powerful game development tool.

1982 GAME MODES


  • Arcade - battle through 50 progressively difficult levels against some familiar early 80's home computer and arcade enemies.
  • Survivor - how many points can you score with only one life?
  • Time Attack - score as many points as you can in 3 mins. Unlimited energy, but each hit reduces your score multiplier

POWER-UPS - Kill, Catch or Collect


Each power-up has 2 uses, one when collected by the players ship and the other when shot and destroyed.
If you catch a power-up before it hits the ground then it's effect is increased. (ie. More energy is regained or lasers, rockets or shield last longer.) A successful catch is indicated by a heart.

Kill, Catch or Collect?

The 4 types and uses are as follows:

1. Energy Power-ups (green)
Kill - creates a large explosion
Catch or Collect - restore player energy

2. Laser Power-ups (red)
Kill - deploys a temporary horizontally firing laser turret
Catch or Collect - grants the player a temporary weapon increase

3. Rockets Power-ups (purple)
Kill - deploys a temporary rotating rocket launching turret
Catch or Collect - grants player a temporary rocket power-up

4. Shield Power-ups (cyan)
Kill - creates a temporary portal that destroys all enemy bullets
Catch or Collect - grants the player a temporary shield protecting against all impacts

SCORING


General
Each enemy kill is worth 1 pt x score multiplier.
The Score Multiplier is increased by filling the kill gauge on the left of the screen. To do this string a lot of kills together quickly. Failing to kill anything causes the gauge to drop.

Abductions...of Man & Multipliers
When a certain number of enemies reach the ground a Man will be abducted by a yellow saucer. As well as abducting Man the saucer takes x3 from your multiplier.

Kill the saucer and allow Man to fall safely to the ground and your x3 multiplier is returned.

The number of enemies reaching the ground needed to trigger an abduction reduces as your multiplier increases. High multipliers are hard to defend.

Coins
Many in game actions such as killing certain enemies trigger a coin drop. Pick up the coins for extra points (5pts x multi), catch them for a further bonus (10pts x multi). Caught coins are indicated by a heart.

Bonuses
Complete any of these in game actions to trigger a bonus coin drop...

  • Arcadia - Survive a level
  • Astro Blaster - get a new high multiplier for your current game
  • Major Havoc - trigger 2 Astro Blasters within 5 secs
  • Missile Command - have 2 remote missile launchers active at the same time
  • Laser Zone - have 2 remote lasers active at the same time
  • Bomberman - kill lots of enemies in an energy power-up explosion
  • Defender - stop any enemy reaching the ground for 30 secs
  • Repulsar - Ram an enemy with your shields
  • 2084 - rescue Man from the saucers 3 times in a row

reviews.review:
1982 is a free retro inspired arcade shooter that feels like it was made specifically for me to pick up and start blasting without having to learn a huge amount first. I control a small ship while enemies fill the screen and I try to survive increasingly difficult stages. The whole thing has a strong early 80s arcade feel, with pixel graphics, familiar enemy ideas and a simple score chasing structure. It is very straightforward, but I think that is part of the appeal because I can get into a game almost immediately.

The main Arcade mode gives me 50 levels to work through, and the difficulty keeps increasing as I progress. I like the way the game builds from relatively manageable stages into much more hectic ones because it gives me something clear to work towards. There are also Survivor and Time Attack modes, so I can switch things up when I do not want to simply work through the main levels. Time Attack gives me three minutes to score as much as possible, while Survivor gives me one life and basically asks how long I can keep everything under control.

The power up system is probably my favourite part because I have to decide what to do with the things that appear on screen. Power ups can be collected by my ship, but I can also shoot them, and catching one before it hits the ground gives me a stronger effect. That makes me think for a moment instead of automatically grabbing everything I see. I can get things like energy, lasers, rockets and shields, while coins and other bonuses give me more opportunities to build my score. I like small systems like this because they give the basic shooting a little more depth without making the game complicated.

The difficulty is where I have mixed feelings. 1982 definitely wants me to play carefully, and once the later stages start getting busy I have to pay attention to enemies coming from different directions while also keeping an eye on my energy. I enjoy that old arcade style of difficulty when I feel like I am improving through practice, but there are moments where the game can become pretty unforgiving. It is not a game I would play for a relaxing experience. I have to actually concentrate if I want to get far, and that works well for the kind of short sessions this game is built around.

The biggest weakness for me is that the basic formula does not have much room to evolve. Even with 50 Arcade levels and the extra modes, I am still fundamentally flying around and shooting enemies. The references to older arcade and home computer games are a big part of the charm, but they also mean the game feels intentionally old fashioned. There is no large progression system, story or character development to give me another reason to keep playing. Once I have seen what the game has to offer, most of my motivation comes from trying to improve my own performance.

I do think the free price makes the whole package much easier to appreciate. I am getting the full game without having to pay anything, including the different modes, power ups, 50 level Arcade campaign and Steam achievements. The presentation is basic, but I think that is appropriate here. It is clearly trying to capture the feeling of an early arcade shooter rather than compete with modern shooters on graphics or complexity. Even the extremely small storage requirement fits the whole lightweight nature of the game.

Overall, 1982 is a simple but enjoyable arcade shooter that understands exactly what it wants to be. I like the 50 progressively harder levels, the different game modes and especially the power up system because deciding whether to kill, collect or catch something adds a little extra thought to the shooting. The lack of deeper progression and the fairly repetitive core gameplay stop me from rating it much higher, but I do not think it needs to be more complicated than it is. For me, it works best as a quick retro style challenge that I can play for a short while, try to beat my previous performance and then come back to later.

Rating: 7/10
